newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines frees jailed leftist leader.
newsitem.headline: Philippines frees jailed leftist leader.

text.p: The Philippines on Wednesday freed leftist leader Filemon Lagman from two weeks' detention in an army camp after a court ruled his arrest was illegal.
Lagman, head of the Coalition of Filipino Workers (BMP), was on his 15th day of fast in prison, taking only liquids, to protest his detention when the court ordered his release.
Soldiers arrested him on November 12 after intelligence reports that leftist groups planned to disrupt the just ended summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum.
The summit, held on Monday at nearby Subic Bay freeport, passed off without any major incident.
"It was very clear my arrest was linked to the APEC summit. Now that the summit is over, they set me free," Lagman told reporters.
The military had said they arrested Lagman for alleged involvement in the killing of a Manila policeman in 1992 and denied it was connected with the APEC summit.
A judge ordered Lagman's release saying the evidence presented by the military against him during a preliminary investigation was insufficient to keep him in custody.

Thousands of leftists staged protest caravans from Manila to Subic Bay denouncing APEC as a tool by advanced countries to dominate less developed ones but retreated after they ran into a heavy police barricade before they could reach Subic Bay.
